hints: Focus on the reaction type here, an alcohol plus a carboxylic acid with acid catalyst means esterification with water lost.
Notice the diol has two -OH groups and ethanoic acid is in excess, so both -OH groups can form an ester linkage.
Build the diester by joining a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$- unit to each oxygen of the $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2-$ backbone and check which option shows two identical ethanoate ends.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Great start, let's see what is happening. A diol plus a carboxylic acid with acid catalyst is esterification.

General ester equation:
$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \rightarrow \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Use excess acid to find the product type**

Here we have $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with two alcohol groups, and excess $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.

That means both -OH groups react, so we get a diester plus two water molecules:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OOCCH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check the formula and pick the structure**

Let's confirm atoms: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2 + 2(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2) - 2(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = \text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_4$. This matches the given formula.

The structure must be symmetrical with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2-$ at both ends of the $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2-$ unit, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCOCH}_3$.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{OCOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ has the ester groups the wrong way round. It is dimethyl butanedioate, which would need butanedioic acid plus methanol, not ethane-1,2-diol plus ethanoic acid.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is unsymmetrical. The left end is a correct ethanoate ester, but the right end $\text{-CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a methyl ester fragment that cannot form from $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
options.C: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCOCH}_3$ is the diester formed when both -OH groups of ethane-1,2-diol react with two molecules of ethanoic acid. It is symmetrical, contains two ester linkages, and has formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_4$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OCOCH}_3$ still contains a free $\text{-OH}$ group and a ketone $\text{C=O}$ in the middle. Esterification only makes esters plus water, it never creates a ketone, and with excess acid no -OH should remain.
